text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- MINIMUM WAGE AND HEALTH SEEN AS STARS IN 1997
At the start of next year, the Brazilian government will announce an extensive program to eliminate slave labor and dangerous child labor on sugar plantations.
-- INCENTIVES EXPANDED FOR BRAZIL'S NORTHEAST
A package of benefits unveiled by the government is intended to benefit companies of all sectors that move to Brazil's impoverished northeast.
-- BRAZILIANS EAT MORE AND BETTER

Brazilians have never enjoyed a Christmas with so much food on the table as they will this year. Accrding to the Brazilian Food Industry Association sales for the industry rose four percent to $63 billion, up from $58.9 billion.
O GLOBO
-- RIO MAYOR SIGNS JAPANESE TRAIN CONCESSION
Rio de Janeiro mayor Cesar Maia has signed a decree grantng K Inada the right to build and operate a new high-speed surface train (HSST) between the city's center and Barra da Tijuca district.
-- TERROR WANTS BILLIONS FOR HOSTAGES, BRITISH PAPER SAYS
The terrorists occupying the Japanese embassy in Lima want a ransom of billions of dollars to release hostages they are holding, according to British newspaper The Independent.
-- CONFUSING SUNDAY FOR ROMARIO
Brazilian soccer star Romario was taken to the police station after a brawl, which started after he elbowed a 16-year-old who was jeering at him during a beach soccer-volley ball match.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- MARXIST GUERRILLAS FREE 225 HOSTAGES IN PERU
Guerrillas of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement freed 225 hostages late Sunday but are still holding on to more than 140 at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
-- SCHEME CHARGES FOR FM RADIO CONCESSIONS
A tape recording obtained by Folha has revealed that a scheme exists that seeks to charge people for granting of new FM radio concessions.
-- CONGRESS DOES NOT WANT RE-ELECTION REFERENDUM
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said Congress does not agree with the idea of holding a referendum on the issue of re-election.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
